#read in VRM data and tidied usage data
```{r, echo =F}
vrm <- read_csv("VRM.csv")

vrm

#open use dataframe saved from anchorages-exploratory.Rmd

anchor_sum <-readRDS("use.rds")


SGI_sum <- anchor_sum %>% filter(main_anchorage %in% c("NANAIMO", "PLUMPER SOUND", "CAPTAIN'S PASS", "COWICHAN BAY", "TRINCOMALI", "HOUSTON PASS", "KULLEET BAY", "LADYSMITH"))
```

# usage data plots for impacts paper
```{r, echo = F}
anchor_sum %>% distinct(anchorage) %>% print(n = Inf)

anchor_sum %>% ungroup() %>% distinct(anchorage)

anchor_sum %>% ungroup() %>% distinct(main_anchorage) %>% print(n = Inf)

#exclude little used, non primary anchorages
anchor_sum_select <- anchor_sum %>% filter(!main_anchorage %in% c("PORT ALBERNI", "PORT ALICE", "STEWART", "ILSTAD", "ZEBALLOS", "KULTUS COVE", "KITIMAT"))

#exclude X PR anchorages and combine Kitimat into one

anchor_sum_select <- anchor_sum_select %>%
  filter(!str_detect(anchorage, "XPRINCE")) %>%
  mutate(anchorage = if_else(str_detect(anchorage, regex("KITIMAT", ignore_case = TRUE)), 
                               "KITIMAT", 
                               anchorage))

anchor_sum_select %>% ungroup() %>% distinct(anchorage) %>% print(n = Inf) # this is 127 anchorages. Of these 109 are in the active databases because active database includes royal roads or sandheads

tot_events_year <- anchor_sum_select %>%  dplyr::group_by(arrived_year) %>% 
  summarize("Total_events" = sum(anchoring_events), "mean_occupancy" = mean(`% of year occupied`), "min_occupancy" = min(`% of year occupied`), "max_occupancy" = max(`% of year occupied`), "sd" = sd(`% of year occupied`))

# add a column with anchroage region and group by that. Regions are Prince Rupert, Vancouver, SGI

anchor_sum_select <-anchor_sum_select %>%
  mutate(anchorage_region = case_when(
    main_anchorage == "PRINCE RUPERT" ~ "PRINCE RUPERT",
    main_anchorage %in% c("ENGLISH BAY", "VANCOUVER HARBOUR") ~ "VANCOUVER",
    TRUE ~ "SG ISLANDS"
  ))


events_by_region <-anchor_sum_select %>%  dplyr::group_by(anchorage_region, arrived_year) %>% 
  summarize("Total_events" = sum(anchoring_events), "mean_occupancy" = mean(`% of year occupied`), "min_occupancy" = min(`% of year occupied`), "max_occupancy" = max(`% of year occupied`), "sd" = sd(`% of year occupied`))


# figures for impacts paper

tot_events_year

  theme_black<- function (base_size = 16, base_family = ""){

              panel.grid.minor = element_line(colour = "grey5", size = 0.5),

             )
    }
  
tot_events_year %>% ggplot() +

tot_events_year %>% filter(!arrived_year == 2022) %>% summarize(total_events_all = sum(Total_events, na.rm = TRUE)) #38681
```

# Impacts paper figure 3 (two panel figure of anchoring events over time)
```{r, echo = F}
#cleaner code to combine the two panels for FIGURE 3 in paper, updated for revision with correct legends


library(ggplot2)
library(patchwork)
library(grid)

ylims <- c(0, 3750)
xlims <- c(2008, 2021)

base_theme <- theme_classic(base_size = 12) +
  theme(
    axis.title = element_text(size = 10, face = "bold"),
    axis.text = element_text(size = 10),
    axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1),
    plot.title = element_text(size = 11, face = "bold"),
    plot.tag = element_text(size = 13, face = "bold")
  )

# Panel A: Overall
p1 <- tot_events_year %>%
  ggplot(aes(
    x = arrived_year,
    y = Total_events,
    size = mean_occupancy
  )) +
  geom_point(colour = "#08306b", alpha = 0.85) +

  scale_size_continuous(
  name = "Mean % of year occupied",
  range = c(2, 10),
  breaks = c(15, 20, 40),
  labels = c("15%", "20%", "40%")
) +

  scale_x_continuous(
    name = "Year",
    limits = xlims,
    breaks = 2008:2022,
    expand = expansion(mult = c(0.05, 0.05))
  ) +

  scale_y_continuous(
    name = "Total number of anchoring events",
    limits = ylims,
    expand = expansion(mult = c(0.05, 0.05))
  ) +

  labs(title = "Overall") +

  guides(
  size = guide_legend(
    nrow = 1,
    byrow = TRUE,
    direction = "horizontal",
    override.aes = list(
      colour = "#08306b",
      alpha = 1
    )
  )
)+

  base_theme +

 theme(
  legend.position = "bottom",
  legend.direction = "horizontal",
  legend.box = "vertical",
  legend.background = element_blank(),
  legend.key = element_blank(),
  legend.box.background = element_blank(),
  legend.title = element_text(size = 9, face = "bold"),
  legend.text = element_text(size = 8),
  legend.key.size = unit(0.6, "lines"),
  legend.spacing.x = unit(0.4, "lines"),
  legend.spacing.y = unit(0.15, "lines"),
  legend.margin = margin(t = 3, r = 2, b = 2, l = 2)
)


# Panel B: By region
p2 <- events_by_region %>%
  ggplot(aes(
    x = arrived_year,
    y = Total_events,
    colour = anchorage_region,
    size = mean_occupancy
  )) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.85) +

  scale_colour_manual(
    values = c(
      "#92c5de",
      "#f4a582",
      "#ca0020"
    ),
    name = "Region",
    labels = c(
      "North Coast",
      "SGI",
      "Vancouver"
    )
  ) +

  scale_size_continuous(
    name = "Mean % of year occupied",
    range = c(2, 10),
    breaks = c(5,20, 60),
    labels = c("5%", "20%", "60%")
  ) +

  scale_x_continuous(
    name = "Year",
    limits = xlims,
    breaks = 2008:2022,
    expand = expansion(mult = c(0.05, 0.05))
  ) +

  scale_y_continuous(
    limits = ylims,
    expand = expansion(mult = c(0.05, 0.05))
  ) +

  labs(title = "By region") +

  
  guides(
  colour = guide_legend(
    order = 1,
    nrow = 1,
    byrow = TRUE,
    override.aes = list(size = 4, alpha = 1)
  ),
  size = guide_legend(
    order = 2,
    nrow = 1,
    direction = "horizontal"
  )
) +

  base_theme +

  theme(
  legend.position = "bottom",
  legend.direction = "horizontal",
  legend.box = "vertical",
  legend.background = element_blank(),
  legend.key = element_blank(),
  legend.box.background = element_blank(),
  legend.title = element_text(size = 9, face = "bold"),
  legend.text = element_text(size = 8),
  legend.key.size = unit(0.6, "lines"),
  legend.spacing.x = unit(0.4, "lines"),
  legend.spacing.y = unit(0.15, "lines"),
  legend.margin = margin(t = 3, r = 2, b = 2, l = 2)
)


# Combine panels while retaining independent legends
combined_plot <- (p1 | p2) +
  plot_annotation(tag_levels = "A") +
  plot_layout(
    widths = c(1, 1),
    guides = "keep"
  )

combined_plot

ggsave(
  filename = "anchoring_figure.png",
  plot = combined_plot,
  width = 10,
  height = 6,
  dpi = 600
)

```

# truncate the VRM file to what we need and clean up the column names

```{r, echo = F}
# rename columns

vrm <- vrm %>% 
  rename(anchorage = `Anchorage name`,
         main_anchorage = Region,
         depth = `Depth (m)`,
         LOA = `LOA (m)`, 
         swing = `Swing Radius (m)`,
         survey_year = LastMultibeamSurveyYear,
         ruggedness_swing = `%of SwingRadiusDisturbedlessNaturalRuggedness`,
        ruggedness_200m = `% of 200 m equivalent distubed Less Natural Ruggedness`, 
        swing_to_50 = `50percent_swingradius`)


# filter out columns we want
cols <- c("anchorage", 
          "main_anchorage",
          "Type",
          "Source",
          "Latitude", 
          "Longitude",
          "depth",
          "LOA",
          "swing",
          "survey_year",
          "Multibeam_ID",
          "TotalSwingRadiusArea",
          "ruggedness_swing",
          "ruggedness_200m",
          "vrm_50percent",
        "swing_to_50")
```


Make anchor events names match between SGI_sum and vrm file
```{r, echo = F}

SGI_sum <- SGI_sum %>% mutate(anchorage = str_to_title(anchorage)) %>% 
                              mutate(main_anchorage = str_to_title(main_anchorage))

vrm <-vrm %>% mutate(anchorage = str_to_title(anchorage)) %>% mutate(anchorage = ifelse(anchorage == "Kulleet Bay Anchorage 2 (Ls9)", "Kulleet Bay Anchorage 2",anchorage)) %>%
  mutate(anchorage = ifelse(anchorage == "Kulleet Bay Anchorage 1 (Ls8)", "Kulleet Bay Anchorage 1",anchorage))

# subset and remove NAs
vrm_sub <- (vrm[, cols])

vrm_sub

```

# pull out the usage stats we need for both total time in the usage data set but also usage stats up to the multibeam survey date year for different anchorages
```{r, echo = F}
# add columns for first year, last year and total years in use
SGI_sum <-SGI_sum %>% group_by(anchorage) %>% mutate(first_used = min(arrived_year), last_used = max(arrived_year), years_used = last_used-first_used)

# realized we need to combine xcow Bay 1 and 2 because they have the same gps location but will deal with this later after SSI


#summarize anchoring events

tot_events <- SGI_sum %>% group_by(anchorage) %>% 
  summarize(total_events = sum(anchoring_events), total_time = sum(Total_time_at_anchor_hrs), across(c("years_used", "last_used"))) %>% distinct(anchorage, total_events, .keep_all = T)

# summarize anchoring events in time prior to the multibeam survey (which are mostly 2022 except for the surveys listed below)
# houstons pass = 2018
# Kullett bay 1 = 2017
# kuleett bay 2 = 2018
# cowichan bay = 2021
# nanaimo 2-6 = 2021

multibeam_year <- vrm_sub %>% dplyr::select(anchorage,survey_year)

multibeam_year <- multibeam_year %>% mutate(survey_year = ifelse(survey_year == "2015/2018", "2018", survey_year))

multibeam_year <-multibeam_year %>% mutate(survey_year = ifelse(survey_year == "2017/2018/2020", "2018", survey_year))

multibeam_year <-multibeam_year %>% mutate(survey_year = ifelse(survey_year == "2022/2018", "2022", survey_year))

SGI_sum <-SGI_sum %>% left_join(multibeam_year, by = join_by(anchorage))

# summarize total hours and total events pre multibeam and for all the years of usage data that we have
tot_events <- SGI_sum %>% group_by(anchorage) %>% 
  summarize(total_events = sum(anchoring_events), total_events_premulti = sum(anchoring_events[arrived_year <= survey_year]), total_time = sum(Total_time_at_anchor_hrs), total_time_premulti = sum(Total_time_at_anchor_hrs[arrived_year <= survey_year]), across(c("years_used", "last_used", "survey_year"))) %>% distinct(anchorage, total_events, .keep_all = T)

SGI_sum %>% group_by(anchorage) %>% 
  summarize(total_event = sum(anchoring_events[arrived_year <= survey_year])) %>% print(n = Inf)

```

merge usage stats with VRM 
```{r, echo = F}

vrm_sum <-vrm_sub %>% left_join(tot_events, by = join_by(anchorage))

vrm_sum


saveRDS(vrm_sum, file = "use_vrm.rds")
```

## making controls zeros
```{r, echo = F}

vrm_sum %>% print(n = Inf)

#change last used date to zero for controls
vrm_sum <-vrm_sum %>% mutate(last_used = case_when(Type == "Control" ~ 0, TRUE ~ as.numeric(last_used)))


#change years in use to zero for controls
vrm_sum <-vrm_sum %>% mutate(years_used = case_when(Type == "Control" ~ 0, TRUE ~ as.numeric(years_used)))


#change total_events to zero for controls
vrm_sum <-vrm_sum %>% mutate(total_events = case_when(Type == "Control" ~ 0, TRUE ~ as.numeric(total_events)))


#change total_events_premulti to zero for controls
vrm_sum <-vrm_sum %>% mutate(total_events_premulti = case_when(Type == "Control" ~ 0, TRUE ~ as.numeric(total_events_premulti)))

#change swing_radius to zero for controls
vrm_sum <-vrm_sum %>% mutate(swing = case_when(Type == "Control" ~ 0, TRUE ~ as.numeric(swing)))

#change total_time to zero for controls
vrm_sum <-vrm_sum %>% mutate(total_time = case_when(Type == "Control" ~ 0, TRUE ~ as.numeric(total_time)))

#change total_time_premulti to zero for controls
vrm_sum <-vrm_sum %>% mutate(total_time_premulti = case_when(Type == "Control" ~ 0, TRUE ~ as.numeric(total_time_premulti)))

vrm_sum %>% print(n = Inf)

# rename the survey_year columns to make sense
vrm_sum <-vrm_sum %>% rename(all_survey_years_forvrm = survey_year.x, survey_year_single = survey_year.y)



#need to fill in NAs from survey_year_single based on all_survey_years_forvrm (these are currenty NAs because the usage data didnt have controls obvs when we merged it)
vrm_sum %>% dplyr::select(survey_year_single, all_survey_years_forvrm, last_used) %>% print(n = Inf)

vrm_sum <-vrm_sum %>% mutate(survey_year_single = ifelse(all_survey_years_forvrm == "2015/2018", "2018", all_survey_years_forvrm))

vrm_sum <-vrm_sum %>% mutate(survey_year_single = ifelse(all_survey_years_forvrm == "2017/2018/2020", "2018", survey_year_single))

vrm_sum <-vrm_sum %>% mutate(survey_year_single = ifelse(all_survey_years_forvrm == "2022/2018", "2022", survey_year_single))

vrm_sum %>% dplyr::select(survey_year_single, all_survey_years_forvrm, last_used) %>% print(n = Inf)

# calculate last year used prior to multibeam surveys, using the total number of years for controls (e.g. 2022 years) because not sure what to put atm
vrm_sum <-vrm_sum %>% mutate(survey_year_single = as.numeric(survey_year_single))
#vrm_sum <-vrm_sum %>% mutate(all_survey_years_forvrm = as.numeric(all_survey_years_forvrm))
vrm_sum <- vrm_sum %>% mutate(years_since_use = (survey_year_single-last_used))
vrm_sum <-vrm_sum %>% mutate(years_since_use = ifelse(years_since_use < 0, 0, years_since_use))

vrm_sum %>% dplyr::select(anchorage,survey_year_single, all_survey_years_forvrm, last_used, years_since_use) %>% print(n = Inf)

```

# removing Naniamo and Cowichan bay from the VRM models as Naniamo is weird substrate and cow bay has so much noise in the multibeam as well as a lot of overlap between new and old anchorage locations making the useage stats hard to line up. Also removing one of the Xladysmith anchorages as it fully overlaps one of the new locations as well but need to add the useage stats from it to the new one
# note we need to remove Xcowichan 1/2 and 3/4 for now as we didn't calculate use stats because they were werid and combined anchroages
# also we aren't going to worry about swing radius for now since we don't know them for X anchorages and haven't decided what to do about those yet
# we will also take out Nanaimo
```{r, echo = F}


#remove nanaimo and cow bay and the Xladysmith one that fully overlaps a new one
vrm_select <- vrm_sum  %>% filter(!main_anchorage == "Cowichan Bay") %>% filter(!main_anchorage == "Nanaimo")

# assign the new swing radii for ladysmith (ABCDEF to 234567) and plumper (C to 4, D to 5, A to 1, 2, 3)

vrm_select <-vrm_select %>% mutate(swing.modified = swing) %>% 
  mutate(swing.modified = ifelse(anchorage == "Xladysmith Anchorage 2", 463.3, swing.modified)) %>% 
  mutate(swing.modified = ifelse(anchorage == "Xladysmith Anchorage 3", 463.3, swing.modified)) %>% 
  mutate(swing.modified = ifelse(anchorage == "Xladysmith Anchorage 4", 556, swing.modified)) %>% 
  mutate(swing.modified = ifelse(anchorage == "Xladysmith Anchorage 5", 556, swing.modified)) %>% 
  mutate(swing.modified = ifelse(anchorage == "Xladysmith Anchorage 6", 556, swing.modified)) %>% 
  mutate(swing.modified = ifelse(anchorage == "Xladysmith Anchorage 7", 556, swing.modified)) %>% 
  mutate(swing.modified = ifelse(anchorage == "Xplumper Sound Anchorage 1", 407.7, swing.modified)) %>%
    mutate(swing.modified = ifelse(anchorage == "Xplumper Sound Anchorage 2", 407.7, swing.modified)) %>%
    mutate(swing.modified = ifelse(anchorage == "Xplumper Sound Anchorage 3", 407.7, swing.modified)) %>%
    mutate(swing.modified = ifelse(anchorage == "Xplumper Sound Anchorage 4", 407.7, swing.modified)) %>%
    mutate(swing.modified = ifelse(anchorage == "Xplumper Sound Anchorage 5", 648.6, swing.modified))
# add usage from Xladysmith 3 to ladysmith B since it completely overlaps
# 
vrm_select %>% filter(anchorage %in% c("Xladysmith Anchorage 3", "Ladysmith Anchorage B")) %>% dplyr::select(anchorage,total_events, total_events_premulti, total_time, total_time_premulti, years_used, years_since_use)
# 
vrm_select <-vrm_select %>% mutate(total_events = ifelse(anchorage == "Ladysmith Anchorage B", 51, total_events)) %>%
                  mutate(total_events_premulti = ifelse(anchorage == "Ladysmith Anchorage B", 51, total_events_premulti)) %>% 
  mutate(total_time = ifelse(anchorage == "Ladysmith Anchorage B", 12545, total_time)) %>%
  mutate(total_time_premulti = ifelse(anchorage == "Ladysmith Anchorage B", 12545, total_time_premulti)) %>%
  mutate(years_used = ifelse(anchorage == "Ladysmith Anchorage B", 7, years_used))

vrm_select %>% filter(anchorage %in% c("Xladysmith Anchorage 3", "Ladysmith Anchorage B")) %>% dplyr::select(anchorage,total_events, total_events_premulti, total_time, total_time_premulti, years_used, years_since_use)
 

vrm_select <- vrm_select %>% filter(!anchorage == "Xladysmith Anchorage 3")


vrm_select %>% mutate(year_last_used_premulti = abs(survey_year_single-last_used)) %>% dplyr::select(18:24)
#plot of VRM200 and VRM swing radius to compare

vrm_select %>% filter(Type == "Anchorage") 

#only 27 anchorages have swing radii to plot (not all of these are perfectly measured as the bathymetry didn't extend all the way so used older surveys to fill in gaps)
vrm_select %>% filter(Type == "Anchorage") %>% mutate_at(vars(ruggedness_swing), as.numeric) %>% ggplot() + geom_point(aes(ruggedness_swing/100, ruggedness_200m/100, colour = main_anchorage, size = swing, alpha = swing), show.legend = T) +
  geom_abline() +
  labs( x = "swing radius VRM", y = "200 m radius VRM", size = "swing radius (m)", alpha = "swing radius (m)", colour = "Anchorage area") +
   theme_classic() 

# 50% of swing radius (removed the trincomali ones where there wasn't enough swing radius)
vrm_select %>% filter(Type == "Anchorage") %>% .[1:34,] %>% mutate_at(vars(ruggedness_swing), as.numeric) %>% ggplot() + geom_point(aes(ruggedness_swing/100, vrm_50percent/100, colour = main_anchorage), cex = 3, show.legend = T) +
  geom_abline() +
  labs( x = "swing radius VRM", y = "50% radius VRM", size = "swing radius (m)", alpha = "swing radius (m)", colour = "Anchorage area") +
   theme_classic() 

# 50% to 200 m
```

#scaling and centering predictor variables
```{r}


#scale predictors
preds <- dplyr::select(vrm_select, 
                       total_events,
                       total_events_premulti,
                       total_time,
                       total_time_premulti,
                       years_used,
                       last_used,
                       years_since_use,
                       depth,
                       swing, 
                       swing.modified)
preds_scaled <- as.data.frame(scale(preds, center = T, scale = T))
names(preds_scaled) <- paste0(names(preds_scaled), "_scaled")
preds_scaled <- cbind(preds_scaled,
                      vrm_select)

preds_scaled

preds_scaled <- preds_scaled %>% mutate(rug_200 = ruggedness_200m/100)


preds_scaled  %>% filter(!main_anchorage == "Cowichan Bay")%>% ggplot + geom_point(aes(ruggedness_200m, depth, colour = main_anchorage)) +
  ylim(0,80)


# more exploratory plots 
# hours, vs events(this one would be a good one to show)

preds_scaled %>% ggplot() + geom_point(aes(total_events, total_time, colour = main_anchorage))

# there is a very strong correlation with a tendancy to occasionally have a few anchorages where there are far more events for shorter periods of time

preds_scaled %>% ggplot() + geom_point(aes(total_events_scaled, total_time_scaled))+
  geom_abline() +
  labs(x = "scaled total anchoring events", y = "scaled total hours at anchor") +
    theme_classic() 
  

# also a weaker correlation between years used and the number of hours that anchors have been occupied on average

  geom_abline()


# plot time since last use (from multibeam survey collection)

preds_scaled %>% ggplot() + geom_point(aes(years_since_use_scaled,total_time_scaled))
```


#Looking at collinearity of predictors to see if we can include both anchor events and anchoring hours
```{r, echo = F}
#Before moving forward, let’s make sure that we can actually include each variable in our model and that we don’t have too much collinearity. To do so, we’ll use the car package. Most VIF calculations were not designed for categorical effects and will often yield super high numbers that might make you think your model is crap - the car package is nice because it applies a correction for this! The only issue with car is that it can’t handle a lot of model types (unlike the check_collinearity() function in performance). So to use it, you can create a simplified linear model with all the same fixed effects and no random effects or non-normal distributions (Paul Buerkner says it’s ok to do this, and I would trust him with my life). - from Bayes baes
#One important thing to note is that if you have more than one predictor in your model, you need to make sure they are not too correlated with one another - if they are, then the model doesn’t know how to partition the effect sizes between them and you’ll likely underestimate their effects. To do this, you can run the model and then use the car package to check the variance inflation factors (VIFs) of the predictors. - from Bayes baes
#
preds_scaled

lm(rug_200 ~ total_events_premulti_scaled + total_time_premulti_scaled + depth_scaled + years_used_scaled, data = preds_scaled)

#issues with swing radius and use because of all the control zeros
car::vif(lm(rug_200 ~  total_time_premulti_scaled + depth_scaled+ swing.modified_scaled + last_used_scaled,
            data = preds_scaled))


# both events and time are above 3 (some people use 3, some people use 5 as a cut off some use 2), a lot of the variation in VRM that they describe is already explained by other variables in the model so we shouldn't include both in the model, I think because we are looking at total disturbance (NOT just drag marks) with VRM that total time at anchor is a much better descriptor than events even though they are correlated

preds_scaled %>% ggplot() + geom_point(aes(total_time_premulti_scaled, total_events_premulti_scaled))


preds_scaled %>% ggplot() + geom_point(aes(total_time_premulti, total_events_premulti))

vrm_select %>% filter(total_events_premulti >85) %>%dplyr::select(anchorage, total_events_premulti, total_time_premulti)

vrm_select <-vrm_select %>%
 mutate(use = case_when(substr(anchorage,1,1)=="X" ~ "used",  TRUE ~ "current"))

```

#making a mesh for the sdmTMB model
```{r}
#add in lat and long to data
 
get_crs(preds_scaled, c("Longitude", "Latitude")) #function from sdmTMB to check coordinates crs


preds_scaled <- add_utm_columns(preds_scaled, c("Longitude", "Latitude")) # add in x and y columns in UTM


# need to make a mesh, required for sdmTMB because it is a spatial package, can turn off when running model though

mesh <- make_mesh(data = preds_scaled, xy_cols = c("X", "Y"), cutoff = 1) #the cutoff is km

plot(mesh)

preds_scaled <- preds_scaled %>% mutate_if(is.character, as.factor)# if you don't turn site into a factor sdmTMB will explode and not run

```

#fitting a sdmtmb model to the VRM 200 m with hours occupied data using a beta regression
```{r, echo = F}

# sdmTMB model fit with a Beta regression


preds_scaled %>% ggplot + geom_point(aes(total_time, ruggedness_200m, colour = main_anchorage))


use2 <- sdmTMB(formula = rug_200 ~ total_time_premulti_scaled + depth_scaled +years_since_use_scaled, mesh = mesh, spatial = "on", family = Beta(link = "logit"), data = preds_scaled, control = sdmTMBcontrol(newton_loops = 5))



# correlation and VIF factor between variables VIF of 3
# spatial field acts as a latent variable to account for spatial effects that are not accounted for by fixed effects


sanity(use2)
summary(use2)

preds_scaled$resid <- residuals(use2)
qqnorm(preds_scaled$resid)

qqline(preds_scaled$resid)

visreg::visreg(use2, "total_time_premulti_scaled")
visreg::visreg(use2, "depth_scaled")



```

```{r, echo = F}

# sdmTMB model fit with a Beta regression

vrm_select %>% ggplot + geom_point(aes(total_time, ruggedness_200m, colour = main_anchorage))

vrm_select %>% ggplot + geom_point(aes(last_used, ruggedness_200m, colour = Type))
# model with events

use_events <- sdmTMB(formula = rug_200 ~ total_events_premulti_scaled + depth_scaled + use, mesh = mesh, spatial = "on", family = Beta(link = "logit"), data = preds_scaled, control = sdmTMBcontrol(newton_loops = 5))

# model with time and years used

use_type <-sdmTMB(formula = rug_200 ~ total_time_premulti_scaled + depth_scaled + Type, mesh = mesh, spatial = "on", family = Beta(link = "logit"), data = preds_scaled, control = sdmTMBcontrol(newton_loops = 5))

use_type2 <-sdmTMB(formula = rug_200 ~ total_time_premulti_scaled + depth_scaled + Type, mesh = mesh, spatial = "off", family = Beta(link = "logit"), data = preds_scaled, control = sdmTMBcontrol(newton_loops = 5))

use_randtype <-sdmTMB(formula = rug_200 ~ total_time_premulti_scaled + depth_scaled + Type + (1|main_anchorage), mesh = mesh, spatial = "off", family = Beta(link = "logit"), data = preds_scaled, control = sdmTMBcontrol(newton_loops = 5))

use_randtype2 <-sdmTMB(formula = rug_200 ~ total_time_premulti_scaled + depth_scaled + Type + (1|main_anchorage), mesh = mesh, spatial = "on", family = Beta(link = "logit"), data = preds_scaled, control = sdmTMBcontrol(newton_loops = 5))

use_use <-sdmTMB(formula = rug_200 ~ total_time_premulti_scaled + depth_scaled + use , mesh = mesh, spatial = "off", family = Beta(link = "logit"), data = preds_scaled, control = sdmTMBcontrol(newton_loops = 5))

use_use2 <-sdmTMB(formula = rug_200 ~ total_time_premulti_scaled + depth_scaled + use , mesh = mesh, spatial = "on", family = Beta(link = "logit"), data = preds_scaled, control = sdmTMBcontrol(newton_loops = 5))

use_randusetype <-sdmTMB(formula = rug_200 ~ total_time_premulti_scaled + depth_scaled + use + Type + (1|main_anchorage), mesh = mesh, spatial = "off", family = Beta(link = "logit"), data = preds_scaled, control = sdmTMBcontrol(newton_loops = 5))

use_randusetype2 <-sdmTMB(formula = rug_200 ~ total_time_premulti_scaled + depth_scaled + use + Type + (1|main_anchorage), mesh = mesh, spatial = "on", family = Beta(link = "logit"), data = preds_scaled, control = sdmTMBcontrol(newton_loops = 5))

use_usetype <-sdmTMB(formula = rug_200 ~ total_time_premulti_scaled + depth_scaled + use + Type, mesh = mesh, spatial = "on", family = Beta(link = "logit"), data = preds_scaled, control = sdmTMBcontrol(newton_loops = 5))
# correlation and VIF factor between variables VIF of 3
# spatial field acts as a latent variable to account for spatial effects that are not accounted for by fixed effects

AIC(use_type, use_type2, use_randtype, use_randtype2, use_use, use_use2, use_randusetype, use_randusetype2, use_usetype)

#checking simulation based randomized quantile residuals using DHARMa, KS test is significant but it looks fine and I think it is because there is a big sample size https://github.com/florianhartig/DHARMa/issues/181
set.seed(123)
s <- simulate(use_randusetype, nsim = 500, type = "mle-mvn")
dharma_residuals(s, use_randusetype)

sanity(use_randusetype)
summary(use_randusetype)

preds_scaled$resid2 <- residuals(use_randusetype)
qqnorm(preds_scaled$resid2)

qqline(preds_scaled$resid2)

confint(use_randusetype)

# real space value of 1 SD time
sd(preds_scaled$total_time_premulti, na.rm = TRUE)


visreg::visreg(use_randtype, "total_time_premulti_scaled", scale = "response")
visreg::visreg(use_randusetype, "total_time_premulti_scaled", scale = "response")

#The package ggeffects can be used to plot marginal effects of given predictor variables in sdmTMB models.

#A advantage to this approach over visreg, is that ggeffects calculates marginal effects with the effects package using the parameter covariance matrix. This is nearly instant compared to visreg, which has to calculate conditional effects by calculating predictions with TMB.

#A disadvantage to using ggeffects is that it will only work for regular linear effects in the main model formula. I.e., it will not work with smoothers (internally these are random effects) or breakpoint (breakpt()) effects.

#Another important distinction is that ggeffects::ggeffect() is plotting marginal effects. This means the effects are “marginalized” or “averaged” over the other fixed effects. visreg::visreg() is plotting conditional effects. This means they are conditional on the other predictors being set to certain values. ggeffects::ggpredict() also does conditional effects, but this has not yet been set up in sdmTMB using the CRAN version of ggeffects.

library(ggeffects)

predict_final <- ggeffect(use_randusetype, "total_time_premulti_scaled") %>%  
  rename(total_time_premulti_scaled = x)


predict_final <-as_tibble(predict_final)

#un center and unscale the predictions
predict_final <-predict_final %>% mutate(total_time_premulti = total_time_premulti_scaled*sd(preds_scaled$total_time_premulti)+
             mean(preds_scaled$total_time_premulti))

  ggplot(preds_scaled, aes(x = total_time_premulti, y = rug_200)) +
  #plot the raw data
  geom_point(aes(colour = use), alpha = 0.4) +
  #now plot the  model output
  geom_ribbon(data = predict_final,
              aes(y = predicted, ymin = conf.low, ymax = conf.high),
                  fill = "purple", 
              alpha = 0.3) +
  geom_line(data = predict_final,
            aes(y = predicted), colour = "purple") +
     labs(x = "total hours occupied", y = "VRM (200 m radius)") +
  theme_classic()
```

```{r, echo = F}
threshold_df <- predict_final %>%
  arrange(total_time_premulti) %>%
  mutate(
    slope = (predicted - lag(predicted)) /
            (total_time_premulti - lag(total_time_premulti))
  )

threshold_df %>%
  filter(slope == max(slope, na.rm = TRUE))

max_slope <- max(threshold_df$slope, na.rm = TRUE)

threshold_df %>%
  filter(slope < 0.5 * max_slope) %>%

threshold_value <- threshold_df %>%
```

```{r, echo = F}
# need to make a mesh, required for sdmTMB because it is a spatial package, can turn off when running model though

mesh <- make_mesh(data = preds_scaled2, xy_cols = c("X", "Y"), cutoff = 3) #the cutoff is km

plot(mesh)

preds_scaled2 <- preds_scaled2 %>% mutate_if(is.character, as.factor)# 

test <- sdmTMB(formula = rug_200 ~ total_time_premulti_scaled + depth_scaled + swing.modified_scaled, mesh = mesh, spatial = "on", family = Beta(link = "logit"), data = preds_scaled2, control = sdmTMBcontrol(newton_loops = 5))

test3 <- sdmTMB(formula = rug_200 ~ total_time_premulti_scaled + depth_scaled + last_used_scaled, mesh = mesh, spatial = "on", family = Beta(link = "logit"), data = preds_scaled2, control = sdmTMBcontrol(newton_loops = 5))

test4 <- sdmTMB(formula = rug_200 ~ total_time_premulti_scaled + depth_scaled + years_since_use_scaled, mesh = mesh, spatial = "on", family = Beta(link = "logit"), data = preds_scaled2, control = sdmTMBcontrol(newton_loops = 5))

test5 <- sdmTMB(formula = rug_200 ~ total_time_premulti_scaled*years_since_use_scaled + depth_scaled, mesh = mesh, spatial = "on", family = Beta(link = "logit"), data = preds_scaled2, control = sdmTMBcontrol(newton_loops = 5))

test6 <- sdmTMB(formula = rug_200 ~ total_time_premulti_scaled + depth_scaled + swing.modified_scaled, mesh = mesh, spatial = "on", family = Beta(link = "logit"), data = preds_scaled2, control = sdmTMBcontrol(newton_loops = 5))

sanity(test6)
summary(test6)
AIC(test, test3, test4, test5)

sanity(test)
summary(test)

sanity(test4)
summary(test4)

sanity(test3)
summary(test3)

summary(test5)

visreg::visreg(test, "swing.modified_scaled", scale = "response")
visreg::visreg(test2, "last_used_scaled", scale = "response")
visreg::visreg(test2, "total_time_premulti_scaled", scale = "response")
```

# SAME USAGE FIGURE BUT FOR BLACK BACKGROUND PRESENTATION
```{r}
dark_theme <- theme_classic(base_size = 14) +
  theme(
    plot.background = element_rect(fill = "black", colour = NA),
    panel.background = element_rect(fill = "black", colour = NA),

    axis.title = element_text(size = 12, face = "bold", colour = "white"),
    axis.text = element_text(size = 11, colour = "white"),
    axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1),

    plot.title = element_text(size = 13, face = "bold", colour = "white"),
    plot.tag = element_text(size = 14, face = "bold", colour = "white"),

    axis.line = element_line(colour = "white"),

    # subtle gridlines for readability
    panel.grid.major.y = element_line(colour = "grey35", linewidth = 0.35),
    panel.grid.minor.y = element_blank(),
    panel.grid.major.x = element_blank(),

    legend.background = element_rect(fill = "black"),
    legend.key = element_rect(fill = "black"),
    legend.title = element_text(colour = "white"),
    legend.text = element_text(colour = "white")
  )
p1 <- tot_events_year %>%
  ggplot() +
  geom_point(aes(arrived_year, Total_events,
                 size = mean_occupancy),
             colour = "#7CFC00",
             alpha = 0.9) +

  scale_x_continuous(
    name = "Year",
    limits = xlims,
    breaks = 2008:2022,
    expand = expansion(mult = c(0.05, 0.05))
  ) +

  scale_y_continuous(
    name = "Total number of anchoring events",
    limits = ylims,
    expand = expansion(mult = c(0.05, 0.05))
  ) +

  labs(title = "Overall") +
  dark_theme +
  theme(legend.position = "none")

p2 <- events_by_region %>%
  ggplot() +
  geom_point(aes(arrived_year,
                 Total_events,
                 colour = anchorage_region,
                 size = mean_occupancy),
             alpha = 0.9) +

  scale_colour_manual(
    values = c(
      "#56B4E9",
      "#E69F00",
      "#CC79A7"
    ),
    name = "Region",
    labels = c(
      "North Coast",
      "SGI",
      "Vancouver"
    )
  ) +
scale_size_continuous(
  name = "Mean % of year occupied",
  range = c(4, 10),
  breaks = c(5, 20, 40),
  labels = c("5%", "20%", "40%"),
  guide = guide_legend(
    override.aes = list(
      colour = "white",
      fill = "white"
    )
  )
) +

  scale_x_continuous(
    name = "Year",
    limits = xlims,
    breaks = 2008:2022,
    expand = expansion(mult = c(0.05, 0.05))
  ) +

  scale_y_continuous(
    limits = ylims,
    expand = expansion(mult = c(0.05, 0.05))
  ) +

 guides(
  colour = guide_legend(nrow = 1, byrow = TRUE),
  size = guide_legend(
    nrow = 1,
    override.aes = list(
      colour = "white",
      fill = "white",
      alpha = 1
    )
  )
) +

  dark_theme +
  theme(
    axis.title.y = element_blank(),
    legend.position = "bottom",
    legend.box = "vertical",
    legend.title = element_text(size = 11, face = "bold"),
    legend.text = element_text(size = 10),
    legend.key.size = unit(0.8, "lines")
  )


combined_plot <- (p1 | p2) +
  plot_annotation(tag_levels = "A") +
  plot_layout(widths = c(1, 1))

combined_plot

ggsave(
  "anchoring_events_dark.png",
  combined_plot,
  width = 12,
  height = 6,
  dpi = 300,
  bg = "black"
)
```
